metadata.boundary: Byte-identity holds only under json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus a trailing newline; the other five dump settings probed all diverge, so a naive re-dump is not byte-identical. Measured on ONE epoch-1 population at schema_version 1.19 whose key order was already sorted everywhere and which carried zero duplicate keys and zero embedded newlines. A state exhibiting any of those three is outside the measured envelope, as is any schema_version beyond 1.19.

metadata.boundary: Measured from --version, --help and config-inspection paths only, with zero billed generation, so every finding is about what the CLI ADVERTISES rather than what it does when driven. Capability rows carrying no probe rule (skills, plan_mode, sub_agents, cache_control, error_class_surface) are declared-only and were not measured at all. opencode was absent from PATH, so all eight of its rows are unmeasured rather than passing. Versions are a point-in-time reading of one workstation's installs.

environment.population: 3 declared runtimes x 8 capability rows = 24 conformance rows; 16 probed against two installed binaries and 8 unmeasured

limits.basis: drift.json installed flag across the three declared runtimes
limits.name: runtimes_installed

limits.basis: drift.json DRIFT rows: session_resume on claude-code and on codex
limits.name: declared_vs_observed_drift

limits.basis: drift.json MISSING rows: all eight opencode rows, binary absent from PATH
limits.name: unmeasured_capability_rows

metadata.surface: installed provider runtime CLI capability surface (claude, codex, opencode)

metadata.boundary: Write concurrency was measured only in an isolated scratch workspace with its own socket path and its own daemon; the live daemon's write path was never contended, so the portalock ceiling is a scratch-workspace number. Head-of-line blocking was measured against a synthetic SYNCHRONOUS handler (1 ping completed during a 1 s sync hold versus 134 during an async hold of the same length) - a mixed sync/async handler set is outside the envelope. Every latency figure comes from one workstation against one 5.7 MB state file.

environment.population: 2,540 read RPCs across concurrency 1 to 64, plus 40 portalocker writers across concurrency 2 to 16, against one live daemon and one isolated scratch daemon

limits.basis: read_ladder daemon.ping at c64: 1280 calls, 0 errors, p95 5.32 ms
limits.name: ping_concurrency

limits.basis: read_ladder state.read p95 507.25 ms at c4 versus 84.41 ms at c1, a 6x knee
limits.name: state_read_concurrency

limits.basis: portalock ladder: 0 errors through c8, then 2/12 at c12 and 6/16 at c16
limits.name: portalock_writer_concurrency

limits.basis: worst read_ladder daemon.ping p95, measured at c64
limits.name: ping_p95_ms

metadata.surface: eawf daemon JSON-RPC under concurrent readers and the portalocker write fallback

metadata.boundary: Measured over the production corpus -- this project's own live epoch-1 .ea tree at cutover, 6,212 rows in the thousands band -- plus nine committed corpora that cover the structural shapes the live one does not exhibit. Ten corpora is the whole measured population: a corpus shape outside that set is unmeasured, not passing. The four legs are dry run, apply, idempotent rerun and rollback over a tree that declared itself disposable, so nothing here characterises an apply against a tree in use, a concurrent apply, or a corpus in the tens-of-thousands band. Two of the ten corpora are refusals rather than imports, and what is measured about them is that the refusal repeats identically and leaves the target byte-identical -- not that the importer handles their content.

environment.population: the live epoch-1 corpus at cutover: 6,212 rows, a thousands corpus magnitude, rehearsed alongside nine committed corpora covering the empty, terminal, multi-root, interrupted, attention-bearing, historical and refused shapes

limits.basis: row census of the live epoch-1 corpus staged at cutover; the thousands band holds from this count up to the next order of magnitude
limits.name: corpus_rows

limits.basis: published epoch-2 generation over staged epoch-1 corpus bytes; observed 0.980 against a declared ceiling of 1.60
limits.name: generation_multiplier

limits.basis: one apply over the live corpus; observed 5.093 s against a 30 s budget
limits.name: apply_wall_clock_s

limits.basis: the generation's own document after the terminal records move to their ledgers; observed 541,112 B against a 1.6 MB bound
limits.name: residual_document_bytes
